hook: The cheapest debt plan often loses.
visual_style: Photorealistic cinematic film still, real materials and textures, shallow depth of field, crisp blue winter daylight, bright white snow, a single red jacket as the accent
world: A snowy mountain in winter today, crisp blue daylight, deep powder snow and dark pine trees
through_line: snow on a mountain: one crashing avalanche, one snowball rolling bigger

cast.Hiker: a woman in her 30s, red puffer jacket, white knit beanie, black gloves, rosy cheeks

props.Snowball: a hand-packed snowball that grows larger as it rolls downhill
props.Cards: a fan of four plain credit cards in different colors with no logos, letters or numbers

places.Mountain: a steep snowy mountain slope under a clear blue sky, dark pine trees below

cta: Comment avalanche or snowball: which one are you using?

captions.hook_line: Avalanche vs snowball: the math says one thing, research says another ❄️
captions.body: Both methods pay the minimum on every debt and send extra money to one target. The avalanche targets the highest interest rate first and saves the most interest. The snowball targets the smallest balance first; research published in Harvard Business Review found focusing on closing accounts kept people going. Education, not financial advice.
captions.comment_prompt: Avalanche or snowball: which one are you using?

youtube_title: Debt Avalanche vs Snowball: Which Wins?

sources.claim: Research: focusing on paying off individual accounts (the snowball idea) helps people stick with repayment

blocks.narration: The cheapest debt plan often loses. Avalanche versus snowball, and why people quit the math. Here is the real reason.

blocks.narration: Both plans start the same way. Pay the minimum on every debt, then throw every extra dollar at one target.

blocks.narration: The avalanche goes after the highest interest rate first. Mathematically, on paper, that always saves you the most interest.
blocks.visual: A huge avalanche racing down the steepest face of the Mountain

blocks.narration: The snowball wipes out your smallest balance first, whatever the rate. Researchers found that closing whole accounts kept people paying longer.

blocks.narration: Close rates? Snowball costs little extra. One card far higher? Avalanche saves real money. The plan you finish beats the plan you quit.
